basis: Bacterial infection umbrella; affected organ sites vary across Burkholderia syndromes.
Tight, inelastic facial skin defines the syndrome; blepharophimosis reported in 1/1. Other facial and ear shape variants do not establish functional damage.
Acute coronary ischemia directly affects the myocardium and coronary circulation.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss occur in most childhood CLN1 cases.
Progressive osteolysis defines this umbrella; extraskeletal manifestations vary by subtype.
Heterotopic tissue occupies the nose and can obstruct the nasal airway; definition explicitly excludes CNS communication.
Mitochondrial disorder with developmental encephalopathy and adrenal insufficiency; hip dysplasia in 1/1 supports skeletal involvement. Dysphagia alone adds no GI axis.
Structural narrowing of the lacrimal punctum affects the ocular drainage apparatus.
Testicular germ-cell neoplasm arises in reproductive tissue; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Congenital duplication directly affects the duodenum.
Inherited aminoacylase metabolic disorders classified as hereditary neurological diseases; neurological dysfunction characterizes the major clinical phenotypes.
Malignant gliomas arise in the central nervous system.
Isolated sperm fertilization dysfunction causes male infertility without a defined endocrine or other covered-organ disorder.
Phenylalanine metabolism disorder spanning benign mild hyperphenylalaninemia to PKU; brain injury is phenotype- and treatment-dependent, with no established umbrella frequency.
Maternal alloantibodies directly cause neonatal glomerular injury, nephrotic syndrome and renal failure.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease. Hearing impairment is annotated at 1–4%; otitis frequency is unspecified. Situs inversus alone adds no cardiac damage.
Keratoconus directly causes corneal thinning, deformation and impaired vision.
Immune-mediated MS and coagulation deficiency define disease; ichthyosis occurs in 80–99%. Optic atrophy also occurs in 80–99% but is omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Congenital cerebral vascular malformation; cerebral hemorrhage and seizures occur in 30–79%. Visual deficits can be central and do not establish ocular disease.
Skin/hair defects, oral clefts/dental anomalies and syndactyly define disease; intellectual disability 30–79%. Hypogonadism 30–79% omitted by cap; respiratory infections are separate.
Inherited abnormal alpha-globin causes methemoglobinemia; cyanosis alone does not establish other organ damage.
Renal magnesium-wasting tubulopathy with electrolyte abnormalities; dilated cardiomyopathy in 6/9 supports direct cardiac involvement.
Recurrent episcleral inflammation is localized to the eye; an autoimmune mechanism is not established for the entire concept.
Alcohol-induced myocardial injury causes dilated cardiomyopathy; liver and neurological alcohol-related diseases are separate diagnoses.
Psychiatric anxiety disorder; palpitations and other panic symptoms do not establish direct organ damage.
